findings.title: Test cleanup removes a provider named "alias" instead of the ones it created.
findings.body: The cleanup is registered as `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, which targets a provider with the literal alias "alias". None of the `idp-alias-N` providers created here are removed. They stay in the realm and can change the IDP counts and cache state that later tests in this class see. The same mistake is on line 425. Fix: capture the real alias, e.g. `String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);`.

held.title: Login IDP cache is not cleared when an organization is enabled or disabled.
held.body: The cached ID set is invalidated only by IDP create, update and remove. If the JPA `getForLogin` query also filters on whether the linked organization is enabled (I could not check that here), this sequence breaks: an organization is disabled when the cache is filled, then someone enables it. Its public IDPs stay missing from the login page until some unrelated IDP change clears the cache. The bean re-checks `isEnabled()`, which only covers the opposite direction (org disabled after caching). Fix: register invalidation of all `cacheKeyForLogin` keys when an organization's enabled state changes or the organization is removed. Or store the cache without the org-enabled filter and apply that filter after reading from the cache.
